title: Hopper Rail: Compact Context Switch and Workspace Reflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The current Redwood Console left navigation becomes noisy on medium and small surfaces and forces an expensive top-level workspace switch flow. Users building multi-workspace dashboards and rollouts report friction when hopping between contexts; repeated clicks, modal context switches, and loss of list context cause metric drop-offs in conversion and debug flow time.

Goal: Design a compact, progressive left rail that: 1) preserves discoverability for docking key routes (dashboards, rollouts, costs), 2) introduces a lightweight "hopper" control for rapid workspace switch without a full context load, 3) gracefully reflows to narrow breakpoints and reduces cognitive load while maintaining one-click access to primary actions.

Scope: Research + high-fidelity prototype + annotated handoff for engineering. Includes IA changes to routing priorities (pin vs. recent), component specs for compressed rail states, and accessible keyboard interactions for hopper. Work includes two prototypes: a collapsed-rail dock with persistent hover peek and a transient hopper overlay that delivers instant workspace previews (name, active routes, last-used dashboard).

Design decisions and trade-offs considered: compact rail vs. hidden command palette; transient overlay (fast, ephemeral) vs. persistent mini-rail (always available but costlier real-estate); keyboard-first interactions vs. hover-first for enterprise accessibility.

Success metrics: decrease workspace-switch median time from 4.8s to <2.5s in microtask study, reduce left-rail width on 1024px+ screens by 24% without lowering feature discovery score, and no regression in keyboard accessibility tests.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype (Figma) covering collapsed rail, peek hover, and hopper overlay delivered and linked
Annotated component spec with tokenized spacing, widths, animation timings, and accessibility labels handed off to eng
Usability test with n>=12 participants showing median workspace-switch time <2.5s or clear plan for iteration
Updated Console IA doc mapping old routes to new pinned/recent model and rollout landing behavior
Engineering sign-off on performance cost (render paths) and keyboard navigation before finalizing rollout plan
comments: 2025-03-13 Marco Ruiz (PM): Nice direction — can we ensure the hopper preserves the current rollout canary context? We need a plan to persist temporary rollouts when the user switches workspaces.

2025-03-15 Sophie Carter (Eng lead): Prototype looks good. Concern about runtime cost of live workspace previews; recommend server-side snapshotting and a TTL-based cache for preview data. Filed ENG-19344 as follow-up.

2025-03-18 Devon Brooks (Research): Usability microtest notes: participants preferred a transient overlay over a always-collapsed mini-rail for rapid switching. Hover peek was underused on touch devices; recommend keyboard and long-press entry paths.
2025-03-20 Lin Chen (Designer): Updated Figma with keyboard-first flows and compact token map. Added an accessibility variant for reduced-motion and screen-reader announcements for hopper open/close.

2025-03-22 Aisha Patel (Creator): Merged final spec changes after eng review and linked design->hand-off document. Proposed soft canary for 5% of traffic behind feature flag. Added release tag console-2025.04.
